paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.
model_annotation: The bar chart titled “DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B Comparison” presents a side-by-side comparison of accuracy (%) between two methods — “Vanilla CoT” (represented by pale yellow bars) and “TLDR (Ours)” (represented by green bars) — across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical y-axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, ranges from 0 to 100 with major tick marks at intervals of 20. Each dataset is represented by a pair of adjacent vertical bars, with the Vanilla CoT bar always positioned to the left of the TLDR (Ours) bar. For GSM8K, Vanilla CoT achieves 92.5% accuracy while TLDR (Ours) scores 91.0%, indicated by a red “-1.6%” label above the green bar. For MATH500, Vanilla CoT scores 86.4% and TLDR (Ours) scores 86.6%, with a green “+0.2%” label above the green bar. For AIME, Vanilla CoT scores 43.4% and TLDR (Ours) scores 43.3%, marked by a red “-0.1%” label. For AMC, Vanilla CoT scores 79.6% and TLDR (Ours) scores 82.8%, indicated by a green “+3.9%” label. The bars are not sorted by height or value; instead, they are grouped by dataset in the order listed along the horizontal x-axis. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or outlines beyond their color coding and the percentage change labels. The chart visually conveys that TLDR (Ours) either slightly improves or marginally underperforms compared to Vanilla CoT depending on the dataset, with the largest gain observed on AMC and the largest drop on GSM8K.

model_annotations.English: The bar chart titled “DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B Comparison” visually compares the accuracy (%) of two methods — “Vanilla CoT” (represented by light yellow bars) and “TLDR (Ours)” (represented by green bars) — across four mathematical reasoning benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (%)” and ranges from 0 to 100 with major tick marks at intervals of 20. Each dataset is represented by a pair of adjacent vertical bars. For GSM8K, Vanilla CoT achieves 92.5% accuracy while TLDR achieves 91.0% (labeled as -1.6% relative difference). For MATH500, Vanilla CoT scores 86.4% and TLDR scores 86.6% (+0.2%). For AIME, Vanilla CoT scores 43.4% and TLDR scores 43.3% (-0.1%). For AMC, Vanilla CoT scores 79.6% and TLDR scores 82.8% (+3.9%). The chart includes a legend in the top right corner identifying the two methods by color, and percentage differences are annotated above each green bar, with negative values in red and positive in green. The bars are arranged in the order of the datasets along the horizontal axis, and no sorting by performance is applied. The visual emphasis is on the relative performance of TLDR versus Vanilla CoT, with the annotation highlighting the small but consistent differences in accuracy across datasets.
